summary_paragraph: The patient, a woman with T1-T2 paraplegia and a history of recurrent UTIs, COPD, and neurogenic bladder, was admitted for hypoxia and tachypnea. She presented with increased oxygen requirements, cough productive of yellow sputum, and hypotension, consistent with septic shock. Imaging revealed severe pulmonary edema with superimposed right upper lobe pneumonia and stable chronic right lower lobe atelectasis. She was treated in the ICU with norepinephrine for hypotension, IV furosemide for acute diastolic heart failure, and broad-spectrum antibiotics (cefepime, vancomycin, azithromycin) for HCAP and a drug-resistant UTI caused by Proteus mirabilis and Enterococcus. Her condition improved with treatment: hypotension resolved, oxygen needs decreased to baseline 2L, and repeat cultures showed no growth. She completed a 10-day antibiotic course and was discharged home with services on home oxygen, her baseline medications, and albuterol nebulizers for short-term respiratory support, with follow-up planned in primary care, pulmonary, and infectious disease clinics.
